reviews.reasoning: Numbering first: web_mt_offset_map.json gives Psalm 127 rule identity (5 WEB verses, 5 MT verses, web_title true), and ps_lib.web_to_mt returns (127,v) for every v in 1..5, so the title pairing web:Ps.127.0 = oshb:Ps.127.1 is exact and no body verse needs an offset. The 2|3 seam holds on independent tier-1 grounds stronger than the row's own signals: the futility catchword שָׁ֤וְא stands 3 times inside the span (oshb:Ps.127.1 words 9 and 18 of 20, oshb:Ps.127.2 word 1 of 13; all three tokens byte-identical to one another) and 0 times in Ps.127.3-Ps.127.5, while web:Ps.127.3 opens with הִנֵּ֤ה on a new subject. challenges.claim: The first observed_substrate_signal labels its evidence byte tier at oshb:Ps.127.1 while quoting no Hebrew at all (0 Hebrew tokens in that field, against 2 in the row's second signal), so nothing in it is collatable, and its clause-position claim does not hold for the MT verse it cites.
challenges.evidence: The signal reads, in straight quotes, 'two paired unless Yahweh...not clauses open web:Ps.127.1 (oshb:Ps.127.1, byte tier)' — the field contains no Hebrew string, so collate.py has nothing to grade; the row's second signal, by contrast, quotes two tokens that do return byte. In oshb:Ps.127.1 the conditional clauses do not open the verse: it opens with the title שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לִשְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה, and the two clauses begin at words 4 and 13 of 20 — אִם יְהוָ֤ה לֹא יִבְנֶ֬ה בַ֗יִת and אִם יְהוָ֥ה לֹֽא יִשְׁמָר עִ֝֗יר, both byte tier against oshb:Ps.127.1. The claim is true of the WEB verse only, “Unless Yahweh builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless Yahweh watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.” (web:Ps.127.1). A byte-tier label belongs to a spliced quote; those two spans are what it would have to carry. Secondary, in the same signal: the two tokens the row does quote, יִשְׁמָר and שׁוֹמֵֽר, are a finite yiqtol and a substantivized participle, so 'the same watch/keep verb appears twice' counts an object the row never names — the shared object is the root, not a form.

reviews.reasoning: Psalm 127 is identity-mapped, so the plain oshb: cites in this row are exact without dual-cite arithmetic, and all 4 Hebrew strings in it return byte tier against the refs they name: the opening clause of oshb:Ps.127.3, the arrows simile of oshb:Ps.127.4, the beatitude opener of oshb:Ps.127.5, and the cross-parent echo at oshb:Ps.120.4 (Ps 120 likewise identity, 7 WEB = 7 MT). challenges.claim: device_notes contrasts this panel with the imperative-warning register of the house-and-city panel, but Ps.127.1-Ps.127.2 contains no imperative form in either witness.
challenges.evidence: MT 127:1-2 carry 33 tokens. The finite verbs are יִבְנֶ֬ה, עָמְל֣וּ, יִשְׁמָר, שָׁקַ֬ד and יִתֵּ֖ן (each byte tier against its own verse) — prefixed yiqtol and suffixed qatal forms, not imperatives, whose imperatives would be pointed differently; the remaining verbals are participles, בוֹנָ֣יו, שׁוֹמֵֽר, מַשְׁכִּ֪ימֵי, מְאַֽחֲרֵי, אֹ֭כְלֵי. 0 of the 33 tokens is an imperative. WEB renders no imperative either: “Unless Yahweh builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless Yahweh watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.” (web:Ps.127.1) and “It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.” (web:Ps.127.2). With no morphology layer in the staged extract, a form label has to be argued from these pointed forms plus both renderings, and they do not support it. The panel's actual register markers are the 2mp addressee לָכֶ֨ם heading 127:2 and the thrice-set שָׁ֤וְא; a contrast built on those would survive the test that kills this one.

reviews.reasoning: The whole_psalm verdict is right and its confidence is calibrated, but the psalm's person-grammar is described backwards in the two fields that carry the warrant. What does re-derive exactly is the closing-formula signal: the last three words of oshb:Ps.128.6 are byte-identical to the last three of oshb:Ps.125.5 — שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל — and that 3-word string occurs in exactly 2 verses book-wide (Ps.125.5, Ps.128.6), so 'byte-identical (3 of 3 words match)' is exact and its disclosure as texture rather than a merge is correct. The title Hebrew returns byte at oshb:Ps.128.1 and Psalm 128 is identity-mapped (6 WEB = 6 MT). One logged imprecision, not a defect: the beatitude quoted in the rationale, “Blessed is everyone who fears Yahweh, who walks in his ways.”, is the WEB text of web:Ps.128.1 but carries web:Ps.128.0 = oshb:Ps.128.1 as its inline ref; check_web_quotes.py passes it under its documented one-verse widen and web:Ps.128.1 sits in boundary_evidence_refs, and the title-pairing form itself is owner-ruled, so I log it rather than file it.

challenges.claim: The rationale describes web:Ps.128.1 through web:Ps.128.4 as third-person description of the man's labor, wife and children, with the voice turning to direct second-person address only at web:Ps.128.5, but both witnesses put second-person address in verses 2 and 3 — and the rejected_alternative rejects the 4|5 break on that same false premise.
challenges.evidence: Sweep object: MT tokens bearing the 2ms pronominal suffix, counted per verse off the pointed bytes. MT 128:2 = יְגִ֣יעַ כַּ֭פֶּיךָ כִּ֣י תֹאכֵ֑ל אַ֝שְׁרֶ֗יךָ וְט֣וֹב לָֽךְ (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.128.2) carries כַּ֭פֶּיךָ, אַ֝שְׁרֶ֗יךָ and לָֽךְ, plus the 2ms yiqtol תֹאכֵ֑ל; MT 128:3 carries אֶשְׁתְּךָ֤, בֵ֫יתֶ֥ךָ, בָּ֭נֶיךָ and לְשֻׁלְחָנֶֽךָ (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.128.3). Across the psalm that is 10 suffixed tokens in 4 of 6 verses (2, 3, 5, 6) and 0 in verses 1 and 4 — final-kaf homographs excluded by pointed inspection, since הַ֝הֹלֵ֗ךְ (oshb:Ps.128.1) and יְבֹ֥רַךְ (oshb:Ps.128.4) end in final kaf without being suffixed forms. WEB agrees verse for verse: “For you will eat the labor of your hands. You will be happy, and it will be well with you.” (web:Ps.128.2) and “Your wife will be as a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house, your children like olive shoots around your table.” (web:Ps.128.3). The psalm's real shape is a 3ms beatitude frame at v1 and v4 — הִנֵּ֣ה כִי כֵ֭ן יְבֹ֥רַךְ גָּ֗בֶר יְרֵ֣א יְהוָֽה, byte tier vs oshb:Ps.128.4 — enclosing 2ms address that begins at v2 and never stops. That shape supports the whole_psalm decision more strongly than the stated warrant does, so the verdict survives; but the description is false as written, and it is installed twice.

reviews.reasoning: Three of this row's factual claims re-derive exactly and one does not. Verified: the title returns byte at oshb:Ps.129.1 (Psalm 129 identity-mapped, 8 WEB = 8 MT); the doubled complaint is described correctly at the codepoint level — רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרַ֑י (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.129.1) against רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרָ֑י (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.129.2) share the skeleton, and the only byte difference across those three words is the vowel of the last word, patach U+05B7 at 129:1 against qamats U+05B8 at 129:2, both under the same athnach U+0591, so 'differing at the byte tier in the final word's suffix vowel alone' is exact; and the K/Q disclosure is right, pmarks_Ps.json kq holding only Ps.126.4 and Ps.129.3 in the 120-131 window, with the inline unpointed ketiv at oshb:Ps.129.3 correctly distinguished from the pointed qere (check_marks GREEN on this row). What fails is the no-shift sentence on which the whole_psalm verdict rests, and with it the calibration of high confidence: the rejected_alternative tests the 2|3 break, which is indeed weak, and never tests the 4|5 seam that the row's own prose marks.

challenges.claim: The rationale's claim that no further address or topic shift interrupts the psalm after the doubled opening is contradicted by the text, leaving the psalm's strongest internal seam at 129:4|5 untested by a rejected_alternative that examines only the 2|3 break — and leaving high confidence uncalibrated.
challenges.evidence: The 1cs complaint voice is carried by 6 tokens, all in vv1-3: צְרָר֣וּנִי and מִנְּעוּרַ֑י (oshb:Ps.129.1), צְרָר֣וּנִי, מִנְּעוּרָ֑י and לִֽי (oshb:Ps.129.2), גַּ֭בִּי (oshb:Ps.129.3), each byte tier against the verse named. It is carried by 0 tokens in vv4-8: those 33 tokens hold only the 3ms pair כַפּ֥וֹ and וְחִצְנ֥וֹ (oshb:Ps.129.7) and the 2mp and 1cp forms inside the blessing quoted at oshb:Ps.129.8. At v5 two tier-1 signals coincide: a new referent group is named, כֹּ֝֗ל שֹׂנְאֵ֥י צִיּֽוֹן (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.129.5), the only verse of the psalm containing the skeleton ציון (1 of 8 verses); and the mood turns volitive, יֵ֭בֹשׁוּ וְיִסֹּ֣גוּ אָח֑וֹר and יִ֭הְיוּ כַּחֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֑וֹת, which WEB renders “Let them be disappointed and turned backward, all those who hate Zion.” (web:Ps.129.5) and “Let them be as the grass on the housetops, which withers before it grows up,” (web:Ps.129.6), against the qatal complaint of vv1-3 and the declaration יְהוָ֥ה צַדִּ֑יק (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.129.4), “Yahweh is righteous. He has cut apart the cords of the wicked.” (web:Ps.129.4). The row's own rationale locates the curse as running from web:Ps.129.5, and the same part divides an equally long psalm at a comparable shift (Ps.130.1-Ps.130.6 against Ps.130.7-Ps.130.8), so the 4|5 seam either carries a row boundary or has to be killed on tier-1 grounds in the rejected_alternative. As filed the no-shift sentence is an unswept absence claim — check_universals.py flags it — that the bytes falsify.

challenges.claim: The rationale mislocates the shared summons: it does not open Psalm 124 — in MT it is verse-final in 124:1, and in Psalm 129 it likewise follows the complaint rather than introducing it.
challenges.evidence: יֹֽאמַר נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל occupies words 8 through 10 of the 10 words of oshb:Ps.124.1; that verse opens with its title שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥ד and then לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה שֶׁהָ֣יָה לָ֑נוּ, which WEB renders “If it had not been Yahweh who was on our side, let Israel now say,” (web:Ps.124.1). The identical three words close oshb:Ps.129.1 as words 6 through 8 of 8, after the complaint רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרַ֑י; the string is byte-identical in both verses (Psalm 124 and Psalm 129 are both identity-mapped) and occurs in exactly 2 verses book-wide, Ps.124.1 and Ps.129.1. The accurate parallel is tighter than the row's: in both psalms the summons stands verse-final in v1 and introduces the repetition that follows, “Many times they have afflicted me from my youth up. Let Israel now say:” (web:Ps.129.1).

reviews.reasoning: The 6|7 seam is well warranted and I support the span: Psalm 130 is identity-mapped (8 WEB = 8 MT), the title returns byte at oshb:Ps.130.1, and the sweep behind the seam re-derives exactly — the skeleton ישראל occurs in 0 of the 6 verses Ps.130.1-Ps.130.6 and in both of Ps.130.7-Ps.130.8, and the 1cs voice of vv1-6 (קְרָאתִ֣יךָ at oshb:Ps.130.1, קִוִּ֣יתִי and נַפְשִׁ֑י at oshb:Ps.130.5, נַפְשִׁ֥י at oshb:Ps.130.6, all byte tier) stops there. Both defects are evidence-hygiene defects that leave the decision standing: a count whose object does not match its sentence, and a quote whose gloss covers half of it. Neither the 145:13 nor the 68:26 rendering zone is in play here, and no selah, paseq, inverted-nun or suspended claim is made (paseq segs do exist in this window per pmarks_Ps.json, but absence of a claim is not a defect).

challenges.claim: The rationale attaches a digit-bearing sweep to a proposition the sweep does not measure: the count (0 of 6 verses at the skeleton tier) is a sweep of the name Israel, while the sentence it supports says the psalm names no second party besides Yahweh — which the row's own second signal falsifies from inside the span.
challenges.evidence: The swept object is the skeleton ישראל, absent from Ps.130.1-Ps.130.6 (0 of 6 verses) and present in Ps.130.7 and Ps.130.8 (2 of 2) — that part is correct and re-derived. But the sentence's object is a named second party, and oshb:Ps.130.6 names one twice inside the span: מִשֹּׁמְרִ֥ים and שֹׁמְרִ֥ים (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.130.6), rendered “more than watchmen long for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.” (web:Ps.130.6). The proposition the evidence actually supports is the addressee claim the row's own second signal states; the rationale sentence overstates it, and the count-object has to be named before it is counted.

challenges.claim: In the second observed signal the quoted span and its gloss cover different spans: four words are quoted from oshb:Ps.130.6 and only the first two are glossed.
challenges.evidence: The quoted span is מִשֹּׁמְרִ֥ים לַ֝בֹּ֗קֶר שֹׁמְרִ֥ים לַבֹּֽקֶר (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.130.6); the row glosses it as more than watchmen for the morning, which covers מִשֹּׁמְרִ֥ים לַ֝בֹּ֗קֶר alone, while the doubling the signal exists to argue sits in the unglossed שֹׁמְרִ֥ים לַבֹּֽקֶר. WEB carries both halves — “more than watchmen long for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.” (web:Ps.130.6). The repair re-cuts the gloss to the quoted span, never the quote to the gloss.

reviews.reasoning: Supported, and the row's central original-language claim is the most precisely stated one in the cluster. Re-derived at codepoint level: the four words יַחֵ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל יְה֫וָה (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.130.7) and the four words יַחֵ֣ל יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.131.3) are identical in consonantal_index.json accent_stripped (4 of 4 words), and every byte difference between them is cantillation in the U+0591-05AF band — U+05A5 against U+05A3 on the first word, U+0597 against U+05AD on the second, U+05AB against U+0591 on the divine name — with no meteg U+05BD in either slice, so 'differ in cantillation alone, not in consonants or vowel points' is exactly right, and accent_stripped is the correct tier to have named. Both psalms are identity-mapped, so the plain oshb: cites are exact, and the cross-parent formula is disclosed as texture rather than a merge, which the two-parent rule requires. The seam itself is tier-1: web:Ps.130.7 opens the psalm's only address to a party other than Yahweh, and 0 of the 17 tokens in Ps.130.7-Ps.130.8 carries a 1cs suffix (the suffixed forms there are the 3ms עִמּ֣וֹ and עֲוֺנֹתָֽיו), so the corporate movement really does not return to the psalmist's voice. Two observations, neither filed. First, the second signal makes an original-language claim — an abstract noun at web:Ps.130.7 against a verb at web:Ps.130.8 — without quoting either token; the forms are פְדֽוּת and יִפְדֶּ֣ה, both byte tier, sharing one root, and quoting them would bring that signal to the row's own standard. I do not file it because, unlike the byte-tier label elsewhere in this cluster, it asserts no tier it cannot support and its content is true. Second, 'Nothing after web:Ps.130.6 returns to the psalmist's own first-person voice' is an unswept absence claim; it is true on the count just given, but the row supplies no digit for it.

The whole_psalm verdict is correct and high confidence is calibrated: Psalm 131 is 3 verses, identity-mapped, and the row-granularity policy puts a short indivisible psalm in one row. The row's original-language evidence checks out. The title returns byte at oshb:Ps.131.1; the le-David sweep is exact against psalm_device_inventory.json, whose le_david membership inside 120-131 is [122, 124, 131], making Psalm 131 the third and the ordinal safe — and the row rightly did not extend that sweep by skeleton alone, since a bare skeleton search for that ascription string across 120-134 also returns oshb:Ps.132.1, where the same consonantal token לְדָוִ֑ד is the object of זְכוֹר and not an ascription at all; the weaned-child simile כְּ֭גָמֻל עֲלֵ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ (byte tier vs oshb:Ps.131.2) is indeed confined to this psalm inside the window — a contiguous skeleton sweep of its three-consonant head returns 1 verse in 120-131 and 9 verses book-wide, a ceiling that still contains homographs rather than a root count; and the closing summons claim is the same accent-stripped identity verified at the paired row, correctly labelled. One further imprecision I do not file: the rationale says the summons ends Psalm 130, where it heads that psalm's closing movement at oshb:Ps.130.7 — but the row's own third signal states the position correctly, so the packet self-corrects, which the comparable slip about Psalm 124 elsewhere in this cluster does not. What I do file is the scope of the length superlative.

challenges.claim: The length superlative is scoped to a production window rather than to any textual unit, and its parenthetical sweep names no unit: at the natural scope of the ascents collection the claim fails, because Psalms 131, 133 and 134 all stand at 3 verses.
challenges.evidence: Verse counts from verse_map_oshb.json across the 15 ascents: 120=7, 121=8, 122=9, 123=4, 124=8, 125=5, 126=6, 127=5, 128=6, 129=8, 130=8, 131=3, 132=18, 133=3, 134=3. Inside the 120-131 window Psalm 131 is uniquely shortest at 3 verses (next is 123 at 4), so the sentence is true only of that window, which is a production span and not a unit of the text; the ascents run 120-134 and there the 3-verse psalms are 3 of 15, tied. The parenthetical, in straight quotes, 'sweep: 3 of 12', also blends two objects without naming either — 3 is a verse count and 12 a psalm count, where the discipline is to name the swept object and its unit before the digit. The decision does not depend on the superlative: a 3-verse psalm with one movement is a whole_psalm row on the granularity policy alone, and restating the count as 3 verses, the fewest of the 15 ascents together with Psalms 133 and 134 keeps every digit true.
